source_row.rationale: ASH diagnostic guidelines use validated pretest probability to guide DVT testing. Low-probability patients can begin with a highly sensitive D-dimer followed by ultrasound when needed, while intermediate- or high-probability patients commonly require proximal or whole-leg ultrasonography. A positive D-dimer alone does not diagnose DVT. The prior item was corrected from the oversimplified instruction to obtain a 'Doppler ultrasound' based only on symptoms.
source_row.source_detail: ASH 2018 VTE diagnosis guideline, reviewed by ASH in 2022 and retained for ongoing monitoring: lower-extremity DVT recommendations 5-8 use pretest probability with D-dimer and proximal/whole-leg ultrasonography; positive D-dimer alone is not diagnostic.
source_row.source_name: American Society of Hematology — Guidelines for Diagnosis of Venous Thromboembolism
source_row.stem: A client develops unilateral calf swelling, warmth, and tenderness after prolonged travel. Which diagnostic approach is most appropriate when lower-extremity DVT is suspected?
